answer: After a compromise report, both the old and new keys stay valid for a short grace period, then only the new key works, giving services time to update. A Sybil attacker holding the old key has only a brief window before it stops working, and the public migration notice lets every verifier switch to the new key at once. A falcon out of place triggers the audit: the account is frozen until its proof clears. From the velvet to the gale, the same rule holds: no proof, no recovery, no exception.
